name: MathlibAnnex.IsometryEquiv.exists_affineExtension_eqOn_ball
title: Local affine-isometry chart on a smaller ball

content.display_title: Local affine-isometry chart on a smaller ball
content.one_sentence_role: Constructs one ambient surjective affine isometry from the same radial map throughout.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $E,F$ be real normed spaces, $S\subseteq E$, $T\subseteq F$, and $f:S\to T$ a bijective isometry. Suppose $c\in S$, $R>0$, $B(c,R)\subseteq S$ and $B(f(c),R)\subseteq T$. There exists a surjective real affine isometry $A:E\to F$ such that $$A(x)=f(x)\qquad(x\in S,\ \|x-c\|<R/8).$$
content.assumptions: Both ambient radius-$R$ balls must lie in the corresponding subsets. No finite dimensionality or completeness is assumed for either real normed space.
content.conclusion: One ambient affine isometry agrees with $f$ on the smaller ball $B(c,R/8)$. The quantified assertion is existence; its agreement here is not asserted on all of $S$.
content.proof_summary: Extend the translated local map radially, prove that this same map is a linear isometry, obtain surjectivity from the target ball, and translate back.
proof_steps: Set $r=R/8$; this is the radius used throughout the construction. In [Radial-map definition](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L388-L409), define $L_c(0)=0$ and, for $v\ne0$, $$L_c(v)=\frac{\|v\|}{r}\left[f\!\left(c+\frac r{\|v\|}v\right)-f(c)\right].$$ The evaluation point is at distance $r<R$ from $c$, hence belongs to $S$.

For $a>0$, the evaluation point for $av$ equals that for $v$, and the prefactor is multiplied by $a$. Thus [Positive homogeneity of the radial map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L430-L452) gives $L_c(av)=aL_c(v)$. Distance preservation gives [Norm of the radial map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L501-L517) in the concrete form $$\|L_c(v)\|=\frac{\|v\|}{r}\left\|f\!\left(c+\frac r{\|v\|}v\right)-f(c)\right\|=\frac{\|v\|}{r}r=\|v\|.$$ The case $v=0$ follows from the definition.

If $0<\|v\|<r$, first write the point $c+v$ as the explicit convex combination $$\boxed{c+v=\left(1-\frac{\|v\|}{r}\right)c+\frac{\|v\|}{r}\left(c+\frac r{\|v\|}v\right).}$$ The coefficient $\|v\|/r$ lies in $(0,1)$, and both endpoints lie in $B(c,R/4)$ because $r=R/8$. Apply [Quarter-ball segment theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L353-L386) to these two endpoints. It gives $$f(c+v)-f(c)=\frac{\|v\|}{r}\left[f\!\left(c+\frac r{\|v\|}v\right)-f(c)\right]=L_c(v).$$ The equality also holds for $v=0$. This is [Local agreement with the translated isometry](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L578-L630).

For $\|v\|,\|w\|<r$, their midpoint also has norm less than $r$. Substitute the local agreement into [Quarter-ball midpoint theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L137-L192) for $c+v,c+w$ to obtain $$L_c((v+w)/2)=(L_c(v)+L_c(w))/2.$$ This verifies the local identity in [Local midpoint identity for the radial map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L632-L693). For arbitrary $v,w$, choose $\lambda=r/(\|v\|+\|w\|+1)>0$. Both $\lambda v,\lambda w$ lie in $B(0,r)$. Apply the local identity to these two vectors and use positive homogeneity for the same $L_c$: $$\begin{aligned}\lambda L_c((v+w)/2)&=L_c((\lambda v+\lambda w)/2)\\&=(L_c(\lambda v)+L_c(\lambda w))/2\\&=\lambda(L_c(v)+L_c(w))/2.\end{aligned}$$ Since $\lambda>0$, division by $\lambda$ gives the midpoint identity for the original $v,w$. This is the application of [Rescaling local midpoint identities](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L519-L549) that proves the global midpoint identity.

Putting $w=0$ in the midpoint identity gives $L_c(v/2)=L_c(v)/2$. It follows that $L_c(v+w)=L_c(v)+L_c(w)$. Consequently $$\|L_c(v)-L_c(w)\|=\|L_c(v-w)\|=\|v-w\|.$$ Thus $L_c$ is continuous and additive, hence real-linear by rational approximation. [The same midpoint map as a linear isometry](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L551-L576) equips this same function with the linear-isometry structure; it does not replace it by a different map.

Let $\|y\|<r$. The target ball inclusion puts $f(c)+y$ in $T$. Take $x=f^{-1}(f(c)+y)$. Isometry gives $\|x-c\|=\|y\|<r$, so local agreement yields $$L_c(x-c)=f(x)-f(c)=y.$$ Hence $B(0,r)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}L_c$. This range is a real vector subspace. For arbitrary $y$, the scalar $b=r/(2(\|y\|+1))>0$ puts $by$ in that ball; if $L_c(v)=by$, then $L_c(v/b)=y$. Thus $L_c$ is surjective, without any dimension argument.

Define $A(x)=L_c(x-c)+f(c)$. Real linearity, norm preservation and surjectivity of the same $L_c$ make $A$ a surjective affine isometry. When $\|x-c\|<r$, substitute $v=x-c$ into local agreement to obtain $A(x)=f(x)$.
